address: Arsenal in Central Park
description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...
short_description: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central P...
title: 40 in Focus: SummerStage through the Lens of Photographer Jack Vartoogian

description_html: Volunteer with the Stewardship team to protect the forested areas in Goodhue Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been funded in part by NYC Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.<br \/>

description_html:
Park Avenue and connecting streets from Brooklyn Bridge to Broadway and Dyckman Street will be open for people to play, walk, and bike from 7am to 3pm.

Our city’s usual traffic noise and honking horns will be replaced with open streets teeming with walkers, bikers, runners, and performers. Discover a wealth of free cultural programs, performances, fitness classes, interactive art, giveaways, and much more as you experience the city in this whole new way.

Route

  • Lafayette Street and Park Avenue between Brooklyn Bridge and East 110 Street
  • East 110 Street between Park Avenue and Broadway
  • Adam Clayton Powell Jr Boulevard between West 110 and West 113 Street
  • Broadway between 110 Street and Dyckman Street

This year's event occurs on July 25 in Queens and Staten Island, August 1, 8, and 15 in Manhattan, and August 22 in Brooklyn and the Bronx.

Visit nyc.gov/summerstreets for location details and programming updates.

Summers Streets is a rain or shine event.

DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics. 

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

Learn more about this event.

description_html: Discover how crochet can support your garden and your community! In this hands-on workshop, you'll learn basic crochet patterns to create useful items, including patterns you can sew in your garden! We'll walk through accessible designs for making plant hangers for vertical growing in small spaces, holders for organizing shared supplies, and mug rugs. You can choose the pattern based on your crochet comfort level! Rooted in many cultural traditions, crochet brings people together to exchange stories and knowledge. Especially during the off-season or on rainy days, it's a mindful, indoor companion to gardening. All skill levels welcome. Yarn, hooks, and materials will be provided.<br \/>NYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation's most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. address: Arsenal in Central Park
description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...

title: 40 in Focus: SummerStage through the Lens of Photographer Jack Vartoogian

address: Reading Room in Bryant Park
description_html: In 1973, the Hong Kong movie Five Fingers of Death opened in New York City and became a blockbuster hit. Within five years, Bruce Lee posters were on the walls of every American bedroom, martial arts movies were blowing up the box office, appearing on TV screens, and influencing everything from Hollywood to hip hop. Here's the story of how a bunch of Asian, Black, and Latino kids learned how to do kung fu and changed pop culture for good.<br \/>Grady Hendrix is the New York Times bestselling author of How to Sell a Haunted House, Witchcraft for Wayward Girls, and many more. His history of the horror paperback boom of the '70s and '80s, Paperbacks from Hell, won the Stoker Award for Outstanding Achievement in Nonfiction. He's a longtime journalist who has covered the Asian film industries for Variety, Film Comment, and Sight & Sound, and is one of the co-founders of Subway Cinema and the New York Asian Film Festival. He also wrote the 2019 Netflix documentary, Iron Fists & ...
short_description: Talks on movies, the culture of cinema, and filmmaking.

description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...

description_html: Amy Dryansky's (she\/her) third poetry collection, Ambergris, is forthcoming in 2026 from Pine Row Press. Her first, How I Got Lost So Close to Home, won the New England\/New York Award from Alice James, the second, Grass Whistle (Salmon Poetry) received the Massachusetts Book Award. A former poet laureate of Northampton, MA, she has also received honors from the Poetry Society of America, MacDowell, Massachusetts Cultural Council and Bread Loaf Writers' Conference. Individual poems appear in Adroit, Harvard Review, New England Review, Orion, The Sun, Tin House, Waxwing and other journals, as well as several anthologies. Amy parents two children and is currently developing community-based workshops for caregivers and grievers. She lives in rural western Massachusetts on Pocumtuck ancestral lands.<br \/>Daniel Tobin is the author of ten books of poems, including Blood Labors, named one of the Best Poetry Books of the Year for 2018 by The New York Times and The Washington Independent R...

Since their formation in 1982, JUST SIXTIES has played at top clubs and has been the opening act for Paul Revere and the Raiders, Felix Cavaliere's Rascals and Jay and the Americans. Masai Ujiri, the first and only African-born president of a North American major league sports franchise, returns to Africa each summer to run basketball development camps. Young men from across the continent overcome staggering odds, with an unwavering spirit, to attend these camps, held in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and Rwanda. address: Arsenal in Central Park
description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...
short_description: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central P...
title: 40 in Focus: SummerStage through the Lens of Photographer Jack Vartoogian

address: Citywide Nursery
description_html: Join the Stewardship team and staff at Citywide Nursery to maintain our plant hoop houses and pot up perennials into larger grow pots. No experience necessary, staff will walk you through every part of the project. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Please make sure to wear proper footwear as the nursery is very muddy and dusty. Space is limited and registration is required. This work is best suited for volunteers ages 13 and up. To sign up a group of 5 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.<br \/>

address: Van Cortlandt Golf House in Van Cortlandt Park
description_html: Join Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland and floodplain restoration. Dates include Wednesdays weekly from August 5th - August 26th. Dates are 8\/5, 8\/12, 8\/19, and 8\/26. All sessions run 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM.<br \/>August 5 and August 12: hand removal of invasive water chestnut on Van Cortlandt Lake, from shore and from boats. August 19 and August 26: cutting invasive common reed (Phragmites) and clearing the floodplain edge. Wear clothes that can get wet and muddy; long sleeves and boots recommended for the August 19 and 26 sessions.<br \/>Meet outside the VCPA offices at the Van Cortlandt Golf House, next to the bathrooms. Tools, gloves and training provided. No experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Registration required. Groups of 6 or more, please email <a href=\"mailto:noel@vancortlandt.org\">noel@vancortlandt.org<\/a> in advance.<br \/>
short_description: Wetland and floodplain restoration with Van Cortlandt Park Alliance. Wednesdays 8\/5, 8\/12, 8\/19, 8\/26, 9 AM-12 PM. Tools and training provided.
title: Wetland Wednesdays: Volunteer Restoration at Van Cortlandt Park

address: Randall's Island Park
description_html: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall's Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall's Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!<br \/>This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: <a href=\"mailto:Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org\">Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org<\/a><br \/>Volunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while v...

description_html: Revenge for the Sixties: Sam Alito and the Triumph of the Conservative Legal Movement is the first-ever biography of Supreme Court Justice Sam Alito, the conservative legal movement that shaped him, and the future of a country reshaped by originalism, by prize-winning journalist Peter Canellos.<br \/>Peter S. Canellos is the author of The Great Dissenter: The Story of John Marshall Harlan, America's Judicial Hero, and the editor of the bestselling Last Lion: The Fall and Rise of Ted Kennedy. He served as executive editor at POLITICO, leading the newsroom during the 2016 presidential campaign, and the editorial page editor of The Boston Globe. He has also been a Pulitzer Prize finalist, a recipient of the American Society of Newspaper Editors award in 2011 for excellence in editorial writing along with the 2022 George Polk Award, Robin Toner Award, and News Leaders Association Batten Medal for his writing about the Supreme Court.<br \/>

description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...

address: Arsenal in Central Park
description_html: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central Park to Marcus Garvey Park and Tompkins Square Park. This selection of intimate, rarely seen imagery gives viewers a look back at past decades of outdoor live music in New York City, a peek behind the curtain with never-before-seen backstage photos and honors those artists who have passed on. From the earliest performances with Sun Ra Arkestra and Mavis and Pop Staples, to legendary artists in memoriam like Tito Puente and Hugh Masekela and backstage shots of Buddy Guy and Darlene Love, this exhibition celebrates not only a photographer's commitment to documenting performance but also celebrates a 40-year legacy of SummerStage.<br \/>This free exhibition is presented by City Parks Foundation in collaboration with NYC Parks Art & Antiquities department.<br \/>An opening reception will be held on June 16 from 6pm-8 pm, ...
short_description: From 1987 to 2019, celebrated NYC photographer Jack Vartoogian captured hundreds of SummerStage performances across Manhattan parks, from Central P...
title: 40 in Focus: SummerStage through the Lens of Photographer Jack Vartoogian

description_html: Bring your 4-legged friends to a special Open Run! <br \/>NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.<br \/>Evidence of Inwood Hill Park's formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.<br \/>St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary's Park received $30 million from NYC's Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park's ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.<br \/>

About Serpentine Sibyls:\u202FRiver Songs and Sea Shanties\u202Fwith Brian Dewan 
 
Artist\u202FBrian Dewan will perform sea shanties and river songs in dialogue with\u202FSerpentine Sibyls, Daniel Rothbart's floating sculptural installation at the Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art at Snug Harbor.\u202FFor approximately 40 minutes, he will\u202Fsing\u202Ftraditional maritime ballads, work songs, and river songs,\u202Fresponding to the\u202Finstallation's\u202Fevocations of the enduring relationship between people and waterways.\u202FPerformed in close proximity to\u202Fthe\u202Fsculptures, Dewan's program will create a conversation between sound and form, drawing connections between folk traditions, mythic imagery, and the rhythms of life on the water.\u202F 
This performance will be followed and accompanied by Daniel Rothbart's Meditation | Mediation project.

address: 196-35 Peck Avenue
description_html:
DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics. 

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

address: Cloisters Lawn in Fort Tryon Park
description_html:
Experience the Sun like never before with local astronomer Novaughn Miller during this fascinating afternoon of safe solar observation. Using specially filtered telescopes, participants will get an up-close view of the Sun's surface while learning about sunspots, solar activity, and the science behind our closest star. This family-friendly program is a unique opportunity to explore astronomy in the heart of Fort Tryon Park.
All viewing equipment is equipped with certified solar filters, making the experience completely safe for your eyes. As the program takes place outdoors during the warmest part of the day, attendees are encouraged to dress for the weather, wear sunscreen, bring water, and consider a hat for sun protection.
Sunday, August 23
4:00 p.m.
Cloisters Lawn

description_html: Join us at Reel Talks for a conversation on Eyes Wide Shut with author Megan Abbott and host Scott Adlerberg.<br \/>Megan Abbott is the award-winning author of twelve crime novels, including You Will Know Me, Beware the Woman, and the New York Times bestseller The Turnout, winner of the Los Angeles Times Book Prize. She is also a screenwriter and the co-creator of Dare Me, the series she adapted from her own novel, now streaming on Netflix. She is currently adapting her latest novel, the national bestseller El Dorado Drive, for television for A24.<br \/>Scott Adlerberg is the author of five novels, including Graveyard Love, Jack Waters, and The Screaming Child.  He has written many short stories and contributes pieces regularly to sites such as CrimeReads and Mystery Tribune.  He was born in New York City and lives in Brooklyn.<br \/>

description_html: Join us in practicing this traditional system of health and self-defense on the Upper Terrace. Derived from the philosophy of Taoism, Tai Chi was designed to develop the optimum degree of harmony between body and mind, as well as between the individual and the natural order of the universe.<br \/>Classes are every Tuesday morning, 7:30am-8:30am, from April 25 to August 28, and are led by teachers and students who train nearby at CK Chu Tai Chi under the direction of Master Hyland Harris. address: Hart Island
description_html: Hart Island is the largest public cemetery in the country and has served New York City since 1869. Hart Island's history is connected to many communities with important stories to tell. During the South Island Tour, Rangers will explore what Hart Island meant to the people who lived there, worked there, and were\/are buried there. Walking the South Island includes discussion of an amusement park, military history, multiple pandemics, historic buildings and more. Join the Urban Park Rangers to hear their history and their voices.<br\/><br\/>Participants are chosen by lottery. <br\/><br\/>Lottery registration opens on Wednesday, August 12 and closes Thursday, August 13 at 11:59 p.m.<br\/><br\/><br\/>Please Note:<br\/>-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Anyone who was not registered will not be permitted to attend.<br\/><br\/>-  If you are selected for the program, you will receive a series of emails confirming your selection and must respond as so...

Bring your mat and water and enjoy one hour of yoga with New York City's top instructors. <br \/>Please register for each class at our website online, or in person. By pre-registering, you complete the waiver in advance and will receive weather-related updates.<br \/>Please present your QR code from your registration confirmation email to the Bryant Park check-in staff. Check-in locations can be found at all four corners of the lawn. Each check-in location is marked with pink barricades or a pink tent. description_html: Join the Stewardship team and staff at Citywide Nursery to maintain our plant hoop houses and pot up perennials into larger grow pots. address: Van Cortlandt Golf House in Van Cortlandt Park
description_html: Join Van Cortlandt Park Alliance for hands-on wetland and floodplain restoration. Dates include Wednesdays weekly from August 5th - August 26th. Dates are 8\/5, 8\/12, 8\/19, and 8\/26. All sessions run 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM.<br \/>August 5 and August 12: hand removal of invasive water chestnut on Van Cortlandt Lake, from shore and from boats. August 19 and August 26: cutting invasive common reed (Phragmites) and clearing the floodplain edge. Wear clothes that can get wet and muddy; long sleeves and boots recommended for the August 19 and 26 sessions.<br \/>Meet outside the VCPA offices at the Van Cortlandt Golf House, next to the bathrooms. Tools, gloves and training provided. No experience needed. Ages 15+ (minors need a signed waiver). Limited to 30 volunteers per session. Registration required. Groups of 6 or more, please email <a href=\"mailto:noel@vancortlandt.org\">noel@vancortlandt.org<\/a> in advance.<br \/>
short_description: Wetland and floodplain restoration with Van Cortlandt Park Alliance. Wednesdays 8\/5, 8\/12, 8\/19, 8\/26, 9 AM-12 PM. Tools and training provided.
title: Wetland Wednesdays: Volunteer Restoration at Van Cortlandt Park

address: Randall's Island Park
description_html: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall's Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall's Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!<br \/>This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: <a href=\"mailto:Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org\">Volunteers@RandallsIsland.org<\/a><br \/>Volunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while v...

description_html: Experience the vibrant legacy of jazz in the heart of Queens this summer! Inspired by the iconic Queens Jazz Trail Map, this free concert series brings the borough's rich jazz history to life in beautiful community parks-where legends like Armstrong, Coltrane, Fitzgerald, and more once called home. Presented by Kupferberg Center for the Arts, Flushing Town Hall, and Louis Armstrong House Museum in partnership with NYC Parks, the Queens Jazz Trail Concert Series honors Queens' extraordinary jazz legacy and community spirit.<br \/>TONY BENNETT CENTENNIAL CELEBRATION! Lucy Yeghiazaryan is an Armenian-American vocalist and violinist emerging as a leading voice in contemporary straight-ahead jazz, blending her cultural heritage with the American jazz tradition. Born in Armenia and raised in New Jersey, she honed her craft through the Jazz for Teens program at NJPAC and is now based in NYC, performing at venues including Jazz at Lincoln Center and Birdland. description_html:
DSNY holds pop-up e-waste and textile recycling events in every Community Board district in New York City.

E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics. 

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

description_html: The Only Plane in the Sky reconstructs the harrowing events of 9\/11 minute-by-minute through the voices of those who lived it-passengers, air traffic controllers, first responders, military leaders, and government officials-creating an immersive oral history of a single shattering day. These first-hand accounts paint the picture of a country realizing it was under attack, and the title reflects the haunting moment when all civilian aircraft were grounded, leaving Air Force One as the only plane left in the sky. Just nine days before the 25th anniversary of the attacks, Graff revisits that harrowing morning, honoring its dark legacy while exploring how those hours permanently reshaped our national identity, America's innocence, and generations to come.<br \/>Garrett M. Graff is a bestselling journalist and Pulitzer Prize finalist historian who has covered politics, technology, and national security for two decades. E-waste items collected at these events include: household and office electronics (computers, laptops, keyboards, printers), smaller entertainment electronics (video game consoles, cell phones, MP3 players), and TVs, VCRs, DVDs, DVRs.

Textile items include: clothing, shoes, hats, bags, gloves, towels, curtains, bedding, and all clean, dry, unsoiled fabrics.

Unacceptable items: commercial waste, air conditioners, household appliances, batteries, lightbulbs.

Learn more about this event.

description_html:
Navigating Housing Court can be daunting. Learn Housing Court processes, types of legal cases, and what to expect. It also addresses how tenants can seek recourse through Housing Court, such as to compel an owner to improve housing conditions. This class does not offer nor constitute legal advice.

Topics covered:

  • How to navigate Housing Court
  • Right to Counsel: free and low-cost legal assistance for tenants
  • Different types of cases: access, non-payment, housing part actions, and holdover evictions
  • Illegal lockouts
  • Where to seek help

This class presented by Housing Court Answers is intended for tenants and property owners.
